name: Tune a guitar by ear
blurb: A small ear-training win with an obvious payoff: you can tune anywhere, and along the way you learn to hear beats between two close pitches.
gear: A reference pitch: a tuning fork, another instrument, or one app note
steps: Tune the low E to a reference pitch, matching it by ear, then verify once with a tuner.
Use the fifth-fret method: fifth fret of E matches open A, fifth of A matches open D, fifth of D matches open G, fourth fret of G matches open B, fifth of B matches open E.
Learn to hear the beating — the wobble between two nearly-identical pitches — and tune until it slows to nothing.
Check with harmonics at the fifth and seventh frets for a second opinion.
Cross-check with chords: a G and an E chord will expose errors the string method hid.
Always tune upward to the pitch, so the string settles rather than slips.
tips: Small errors compound down the strings. Check with chords at the end, every time.
The beating is the real signal. Once you hear it you cannot un-hear it.
proof: You tune from a single reference pitch and a tuner then confirms every string within a few cents.
